actions.title: Prepare a numbered board attempt
actions.instruction: From a clean main branch at your Academy clone root, run Prepare in a native terminal. The branch number printed by Academy is evidence metadata; do not type ATTEMPT_NUMBER literally.
actions.rationale: Prepare creates one isolated, reconstructable attempt from the scenario baseline.
actions.recovery: If Prepare stops, keep its message and resolve the named branch or clean-worktree condition. Do not force-reset main or delete an existing attempt.
actions.evidence: All F03 evidence stays on the numbered attempt branch.

actions.title: Read the exact queued task
actions.instruction: Read the board before changing it. Locate academy.feature.0001 and name its description, Done when condition, Boundaries, and Evidence link. This lesson changes only its lifecycle; it does not implement the ticket-list feature.
actions.rationale: A task identifier is not enough: its surrounding scope is the boundary that prevents an accidental feature change.

variants.command: Open .codearbiter/open-tasks.md. For academy.feature.0001, report its description, Done when condition, Boundaries, and Evidence link. Do not edit or commit anything.
Open .codearbiter/open-tasks.md. For academy.feature.0001, report its description, Done when condition, Boundaries, and Evidence link. Do not edit or commit anything.
Open .codearbiter/open-tasks.md. For academy.feature.0001, report its description, Done when condition, Boundaries, and Evidence link. Do not edit or commit anything.

actions.expected_result: You can state that academy.feature.0001 is the only task to transition and that its feature work remains out of scope.
actions.recovery: If the target is not queued, stop. You are not on a clean F03 attempt; preserve that state and use Reset if a retry is needed.
actions.evidence: The final diff preserves every word of the target task except its lifecycle marker and done date.

actions.title: Let CodeArbiter start the target
actions.instruction: In the selected CodeArbiter harness, paste the copied host-native start command into the harness prompt and send it after the learner has identified the target. It is not a shell command, so it never begins with !. The agent performs the sanctioned transition.
actions.rationale: The task writer performs the sanctioned queued-to-in-progress transition and supplies its real date.
actions.expected_result: The target line becomes [~] and carries a real started YYYY-MM-DD date; no other task changes.
actions.recovery: If the command blocks, preserve its finding. Do not hand-edit a checkbox, skip straight to done, or substitute git commands for the task writer.
actions.evidence: The learner observes the live [~] state before completion.

actions.title: Inspect the live started state
actions.instruction: Inspect the working-tree board diff. Confirm academy.feature.0001 is [~] with a started date before asking CodeArbiter to complete it.
actions.rationale: The start state is an observed live transition; after done, the final board intentionally retains only the completion state.
actions.expected_result: The diff shows one target line changing from [ ] to [~] with its started date.
actions.recovery: If any other line changed, do not commit. Preserve the attempt and use Reset for a new numbered attempt.
actions.evidence: You saw the sanctioned start transition rather than assuming it happened.

actions.title: Let CodeArbiter complete the target
actions.instruction: In the selected CodeArbiter harness, paste the copied host-native done command into the harness prompt and send it. It is not a shell command. The agent performs the completion after the learner has observed the started state; the task writer rejects a queued-to-done shortcut.
actions.rationale: Completion records the same task as done with a real date while retaining its scope and evidence text.
actions.expected_result: The target becomes [x] with (done YYYY-MM-DD), using the date written by CodeArbiter.
actions.recovery: If the command blocks, preserve the message. Do not edit a date, amend a prior attempt, or manufacture an audit event.
actions.evidence: The final board line contains the original task body plus one canonical done date.

actions.title: Confirm the one-line final diff
actions.instruction: Inspect whole-worktree status and the final board diff before staging. Status must print nothing except the intended board change; the board diff must show exactly academy.feature.0001 changing from queued to done with its description and child lines unchanged.
actions.rationale: The visible diff is the learner's chance to catch scope drift before it becomes durable evidence.

variants.command: git status --short; git diff --check; git diff -- .codearbiter/open-tasks.md
git status --short && git diff --check && git diff -- .codearbiter/open-tasks.md
git status --short && git diff --check && git diff -- .codearbiter/open-tasks.md

actions.expected_result: Git reports no whitespace errors and prints one queued-to-done target-line change.
actions.recovery: If the diff contains another path or another board line, stop before staging and preserve the attempt for recovery.
actions.evidence: Only the target lifecycle changes before the governed commit.

actions.title: Stage only the board
actions.instruction: Stage the one approved board path. The double dash ends option parsing and makes the intended commit boundary explicit.
actions.rationale: Path-scoped staging keeps unrelated work out of the lesson's one evidence commit.
actions.recovery: If another path is staged, do not commit. Unstage only that unintended path, then inspect the boundary again.
actions.evidence: The index matches the exact one-file evidence contract.

actions.title: Approve the exact commit boundary
actions.instruction: Paste this as a request to the active harness. It is not a shell command and never begins with !. The agent must check the whole worktree as well as the staged boundary before the learner approves.
actions.rationale: The learner approves the board-only evidence boundary before CodeArbiter commits it.

variants.command: Show git status --short, the staged path list, and staged diff. Do not commit. Report whether the whole worktree contains only the intended board change, whether the staged path is exactly .codearbiter/open-tasks.md, and whether the only changed board line is academy.feature.0001 moving from [ ] to [x] with its original body and one done date.

actions.expected_result: The agent presents exactly .codearbiter/open-tasks.md as the staged path and one canonical target-line change for approval.
actions.recovery: If the report names any other path or board edit, do not approve. Preserve and correct only that boundary before reviewing again.
actions.evidence: The learner approved the exact board-only commit boundary.

actions.title: Let CodeArbiter commit the board evidence
actions.instruction: After the learner approves the staged boundary, paste the copied host-native commit command into the selected harness prompt and send it. It is not a shell command. The agent runs the CodeArbiter commit gate; do not use git commit or a shell exclamation mark.
actions.rationale: The commit gate records the approved evidence through the same governed path the course teaches.
actions.expected_result: CodeArbiter creates exactly one learner commit after Prepare, containing only .codearbiter/open-tasks.md.
actions.recovery: If the gate blocks, keep the finding and resolve the named boundary issue. Do not bypass, direct-commit, or amend a different attempt.
actions.evidence: The attempt has exactly one learner commit whose only changed path is .codearbiter/open-tasks.md.

actions.title: Confirm the attempt is clean
actions.instruction: After the governed evidence commit, inspect short status before Check.
actions.rationale: Check accepts committed evidence only when the whole worktree and index are clean.
actions.recovery: If Git prints any path, preserve the commit and resolve or safely preserve that uncommitted path before Check.
actions.evidence: The worktree and index match the one-commit attempt head.

actions.title: Run the external Academy Check
actions.instruction: Use the installed Academy command in a native terminal. Check reads the prepared baseline, committed attempt head, commit boundary, and live worktree from outside the learner flow.
actions.rationale: External verification proves the finished board state and evidence boundary can be reconstructed later.
actions.expected_result: Check prints checkpoint F03-work-the-board: passed; progress: .academy/progress.json.
actions.recovery: If Check fails, preserve the clean committed attempt and read the named predicate. Reset creates a new numbered attempt without erasing the failed one.
actions.evidence: Only a passing external Check records F03 progress.

actions.title: Create a preserved numbered retry
actions.instruction: Use this only when F03 needs another attempt. Run Reset from a native terminal at the Academy clone root.
actions.rationale: Reset preserves the old attempt and prepares the next unused attempt number.
actions.expected_result: Academy archives the prior attempt and prints the next academy/F03-work-the-board/ATTEMPT_NUMBER branch.
actions.recovery: If Reset stops, preserve its message and current branch. Never force-reset or delete the prior attempt.
actions.evidence: The retry starts clean while the earlier route remains reachable.

actions.title: Return to main after success
actions.instruction: After Check passes, return to main without deleting the completed attempt branch.
actions.rationale: The completed branch remains available as durable, reviewable lesson evidence.
actions.expected_result: Git switches to main and leaves academy/F03-work-the-board/ATTEMPT_NUMBER reachable.
actions.recovery: If Git refuses because work is uncommitted, stop and preserve it. Do not force the switch.
actions.evidence: The completed evidence remains separated from main.
